title: Alva, Seeker of the Spurned
snippet:
Alva, Seeker of the Spurned -  Dark Souls III - character - locations 
 locations : He will invade on the cliffside before reaching Irithyll Dungeon, as soon as the player leaves the manor's doorway.

He can be later encountered in the Ringed City as the player approaches an alleyway with a lootable corpse, which is found past a single Ringed Knight.

title: Alva, Seeker of the Spurned
snippet: In the Ringed City, he'll use most of the same strategies, now without the risk of either him or the player falling to their deaths. However, one must be aware of the Ringed Knight who patrols the area, who may give them trouble during the encounter if he is ran past and not dealt with before it's initiated. Since the dark spirit will stay put until the player enters his line of sight, there's no danger he will attack prematurely, even if the invasion has already started. Unlike in the base game, Alluring Skulls won't have any effect on him.

title: Alva, Seeker of the Spurned
snippet:
Alva, Seeker of the Spurned -  Dark Souls III - character - plot 
 plot : Alva is an optional encounter that can be battled if the player is a Host of Embers in his invasion area found between Irithyll of the Boreal Valley and its homonymous dungeon. He must be defeated before killing Yhorm the Giant, as that will prevent him from invading any longer. If the player is successful, they'll earn his weapon, the Murakumo, and his armor set, situated on a corpse that will appear in the lower level of the dungeon, just in front of Karla's cell.

Unlike his base game counterpart, *The Ringed City DLC's* Seeker of the Spurned will invade the player regardless of if they are a Host of Embers or not, a trait shared with other dark spirits in this expansion. Defeating him here nets them the Wolf Ring +3 and allows them easier access to the corpse he was guarding, which holds the Black Witch Set.

title: Alva, Seeker of the Spurned
snippet:
Alva, Seeker of the Spurned -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : Alva is a renowned wandering knight who is very popular among troubadours, who sing the tales of his many tragic adventures, which also involve the figures of Saint Serreta and Zullie the Witch. Eventually, Alva ceased his aimless wayfaring, equipped a peculiar eastern blade, and began a search for the spurned in a journey with seemingly no end. This led him to the forsaken prison of Irithyll, where Karla, a spurned child of the Abyss, had been locked away. The knight seemed to be interested in the witch, possibly even wishing to protect her. This puts him at odd with the Ashen One, who is forced to engage him in a battle and vanquish him, causing him to seemingly perish near the poor witch's cell.

title: Alva, Seeker of the Spurned
snippet:
Alva, Seeker of the Spurned -  Dark Souls III - character - strategy 
 strategy : Alva will mostly attack by performing his weapon's Spin Slash skill if the player wishes to fight him at close range. However, he will start loading his crossbow if they run away, firing Standard Bolts at the player if they choose to remain at a distance. One must be especially careful when fighting on the stairs leading to Irithyll Dungeon, as his attacks can potentially knock players off. Conversely, players can use this against him as well, and Alluring Skulls thrown at the edge of the precipice can prove quite useful to dispatch him quickly, as he'll leap after them, to his death.

title: Alva, Seeker of the Spurned
snippet:
This, however, was not the end for the Seeker of the Spurned, now nameless, as he is later encountered in the Ringed City of legend, long after the events of Irithyll Dungeon. It seems that his journey had ended there, where he had finally found the one he was looking for. Unfortunately, his beloved had been dead all along, and the knight could do nothing more than protect her resting place from anyone who'd dare loot her remains. Once again the Ashen One would battle the knight, conquering the ordeal and slaying him for good.

However, the White-Faced Locusts preach of a way for the lovers to be reunited in the Abyss, though their words are hard to fully trust.

title: Assassin (class)
snippet:
The Assassin Set has only moderate physical defences but has good magic and fire defences, and high overall resistances against anything that isn't Bleed.

While the **Assassin** doesn't have any ranged attack, its Spook Sorcery is extremely useful for removing most non-fatal fall damage and for completely silencing footsteps for 20 seconds, allowing certain obstacles to be bypassed . Unfortunately, while the starting Sorcerer's Staff is a fairly good spell tool, if not exactly the best, it won't actually start to gain scaling from stats until Intelligence has reached at least 19, delaying a possible strengthening of the character's Sorceries.

Picking up the Soul Arrow Sorcery from the Shrine Handmaid gives a reusable ranged attack early on, while the weapon buffing Magic Weapon Sorcery can be gained in either Undead Settlement or Road of Sacrifices to add some of a Staff's spellbuff to weapon damage.

title: Assassin (class)
snippet:
Assassin (class) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Assassin** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It is a Dexterity-based class with decent Attunement for Weapon Arts and spells and some Intelligence for Sorceries.

An unusually long Thrusting Sword, the Estoc is also quite strong and has a rare sweeping heavy attack for hitting several or agile foes easier, at the cost of not having an increased critical modifier for Ripostes and Backstabs. Additionally, its Weapon Art, Shield Splitter, helps with its bad damage to the stamina of blocking targets by partially bypassing the defences of the block instead.

Its Targeting Shield, while not very suitable for blocking, is one of the game's three parrying shields and as such its Parry starts slightly earlier yet ends as late as the regular parry.

The Assassin Set has only moderate physical defences but has good magic and fire defences, and high overall resistances against anything that isn't Bleed.

title: Assassin (class)
snippet:
Assassin (class) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - trivia 
 trivia : This class is fairly popular amongst speedrunners thanks to Spook making it possible to easier skip foes and falls.
While the Assassin doesn't have any direct equivalent class in the Dark Souls series, it does bear some resemblance to the Royalty class from FromSoftware's previous game Demon's Souls, another Dexterity/Intelligence-based class wielding a thrusting sword (in that case a Rapier) and a small shield while also providing access to a Sorcery-like spell (though in the Royalty's case it is the offensive Soul Arrow, not a self-buffing spell).

snippet:

 locations : Basilisks are found in the Farron Keep, near the Golden Scroll and the Antiquated Set.

Further into the game, the player will find a sewer in the Irithyll Dungeon with two chests, one being a Mimic; the normal chest contains the Old Cell Key. After obtaining the item, the player will be ambushed by several basilisks.

The final place that basilisks reside in is down in the lower levels of Smouldering Lake, just before being attacked by Knight Slayer Tsorig near a large pool of lava.

title: Basilisk (Dark Souls III)
snippet: As they are rarely encountered in situations where they are mixed alongside other enemy types, it is best to be patient and slowly but methodically clear out Basilisk nests before moving on. So long as attention is paid to Curse buildup and no additional enemies join the fray, Basilisks can be safely dispatched.

title: Basilisk (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Basilisk (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Basilisks are very slippery foes that can be hard to kill due to their evasiveness. Because they only possess breath attacks, they are incapable of damaging the player in any way short of inflicting the status effect.

Ideally, Basilisks should be engaged in a situation where the player has mobility options. Simply attack and kill a Basilisk while attempting to stay outside of the mist, and retreat as needed if Curse buildup becomes too high. Large weapons with high impact and stagger can lock down Basilisks long enough to finish them off. While weapons with horizontal sweep can allow the player to hit multiple targets at once, vertically attacking weapons can sometimes knock them out of the air as they perform pouncing attacks or jumping retreats.

title: Boreal Outrider Knight

Boreal Outrider Knight -  Dark Souls III - enemy - lore 
 lore : The Outrider Knights are distant descendants of the ancient gods. They were among the Irithyllians, hybrids between the race of the gods of Anor Londo and humans, who inhabit Irithyll of the Boreal Valley, the city built for them on the ruins of Anor Londo. After Sulyvahn imprisoned Dark Sun Gwyndolin, proclaimed himself pontiff and assumed control of the city, they were ordered to serve under the tyrant as Outrider Knights in foreign campaigns, equivalent to being exiled.

title: Boreal Outrider Knight
snippet:
The one encountered in the Undead Settlement can be killed quite easily. Once reaching the bottommost area via an elevator, the player needs to send it back up to leave open a hole in the ground. They may then lure the Outrider Knight near it and run around it until he falls to his doom. The player will automatically receive the Irithyll Straight Sword upon his demise. An alternative strategy is to pass through the door leading to the Road of Sacrifices and killing it with ranged attacks from a safe spot.

They are able to be parried and riposted, however, this can be tricky because they attack with such great speed.

title: Boreal Outrider Knight
snippet:
Boreal Outrider Knight -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Outrider Knights are usually initially unaware of the player, so use this opportunity to start the fight with a powerful attack. Once provoked, it is possible to wear them down with ranged weapons from a distance; however, they can close the gap very quickly so caution is advised. Unless the player has plenty of poise, it is recommended to evade their attacks rather than block them, as they rapidly drain stamina.

All of their attacks inflict Frost damage and can cause frostbite, which can be lethal if the player is unable to escape. They are very agile opponents and will often sidestep attacks, so a quick-use weapon is recommended.

When they are far away from the player, they are very susceptible to ranged attacks and will just continue approaching very slowly without attacking. Headshots are especially effective and will stagger them heavily.

title: Boreal Outrider Knight
snippet:

 trivia : The Outrider Knight in Lothric Castle wields an Irithyll Straight Sword, despite dropping the Irithyll Rapier upon death.

title: Boreal Outrider Knight
snippet: After Prince Lothric refused to link the First Flame and his kingdom fell into ruin due to various internal problems, Sulyvahn would order a division of the Outrider Knights to reach Lothric, under the watchful eye of Vordt of the Boreal Valley. Here they would position themselves in various strategic points of the city, infiltrating the barracks of the Lothric army, the Grand Archives and the Undead Settlement located outside the walls, effectively controlling the places of command and movement of the kingdom.

title: Boreal Outrider Knight
snippet: The pontiff experimented on these knights, giving them his eye rings. While these rings would boost their attacks and recover their health as long as their fighting persists, those who peered inside the black orbs would be lured into visions of endless deadly battles and go insane, transformed into frenzied beasts. The effect of the rings, whose black eyes constantly hound the knights, continues over time, first fusing their armor with their own hide and then devolving them into literal beasts under total control of the Pontiff. These knights, before being dispatched to foreign lands, were given these rings with the power to transform them into savage, raving warriors who only knew how to serve as mindless guards, ensuring Sulyvahn's total control over them and depriving any means of desertion.

title: Cage Spider
snippet:
Cage Spider -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Cage Spiders, on account of their cages, are resistant to slash and strike attacks, but vulnerable to thrust attacks and fire. Although they do not inflict much damage, their erratic flailing attacks can be frustrating when trying to kill them with short-range weapons due to the fact they easily stagger you. They are best fought with spears, throwing knives, firebombs, or pyromancies.

Dormant cage spiders can be easily revealed by locking on to them.

Several are found hanging from the ceiling of the house past the Demon. They will drop and attack if the player picks up the item they guard. They can be identified from dead ones by locking on to them, dealt with one by one by aggroing them with ranged attacks.

title: Sieglinde of Catarina
snippet: **Other details suggest that, in the final version of the game, Sieglinde is intended to be Undead. The player can steal 10 Humanity from Sieglinde with the Dark Hand, and only an Undead would have reason to hold more than a single Humanity. Her continued affection for Siegmeyer suggests that Catarina may not hate Undead as much as other regions. Also, it is implausible that an ordinary Human could traverse the Great Hollow and reach the bottom of Ash Lake without being killed.

As Patches has stolen his armor, the player must retrieve it in order to rescue Siegward. The armor can be obtained by purchasing it from Patches, or by killing him and looting it. If the player missed Patches's encounter in the Cathedral, they must trigger his appearance at Firelink Shrine. The triggering flag for Patches's encounter event is opening the large double doors to the rooftop mausoleum, so opening these doors will cause Patches to sell the armor at Firelink Shrine.

When the player returns the armor to Siegward, he will teach them the "Rejoice" gesture.

title: Catarina
snippet: At a certain point Catarina came into contact, on a conflict or diplomatic level, with the Profaned Capital, and Yhorm the Giant, the ruler of the city became a great friend of the knight Siegward. Before facing his fate as a Lord of Cinder and linking the First Flame, Yhorm made Siegward promise to kill him if he were ever exhumed from his grave, gifting him a weapon capable of killing him easily.

title: Sieglinde of Catarina
snippet:
Sieglinde of Catarina -  Dark Souls - character - trivia 
 trivia : The name Sieglinde is likely a reference a character of that name in Wagner's *Die Walküre*, a German opera inspired by Norse mythology.
Unlike most other NPCs, Sieglinde may not be Undead. In the text dump, Siegmeyer laments the fact that Sieglinde came all the way to Lordran to find him, and that such an action is dangerous due to her status as a "normal" human. After she completes her quest, Sieglinde mentions that she is "returning to Catarina"—one of the few places that is never mentioned to be undead. Since the undead and hollow are abhorred by the rest of the world, she would not otherwise be able to return to her home, unless she herself was not undead.

snippet:

title: Greirat of the Undead Settlement
snippet:
At this point, the player must defeat an area boss in order for Greirat to return safely. The three earliest bosses available to accomplish this are the Curse-rotted Greatwood, Pontiff Sulyvahn, and the Old Demon King. If the player kills Emma they can also defeat any of the available bosses within Lothric Castle, and any boss in Ashes of Ariandel or The Ringed City is also an option provided that they are accessible.

If Greirat dies during this part of his questline, the player can retrieve his ashes from his body located in the far-right corner of the left path in the sewers of Irithyll, surrounded by three Sewer Centipedes. Bring the ashes to the Shrine Handmaid and she will update her stock of wares with those Greirat initially sold, as well as those that he would have sold had he returned alive.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
The Ashen One may also rescue Cornyx of the Great Swamp, a master of pyromancy who will offer his teachings to the Ashen One. Upon finding the church in the center of the settlement, the Ashen One encounters Eygon of Carim, a disdainful knight of Carim. If the Ashen One purchases a key from the handmaiden, they may free Eygon's ward, a blind nun by the name of Irina, who will offer to tell the Ashen One stories of miracles. After freeing her, Eygon will offer an alliance to the Ashen One, for as long as Irina's safety is guaranteed.

Inside the church, the Ashen One encounters Siegward of Catarina, a Catarina knight who is perplexed by a lift that will only take him down, rather than up where he wishes to speak to the Giant. If the Ashen One solves the riddle of the lift, they may make peace with the Giant, who will offer his help.

Once through the settlement, the Ashen One makes it to the Road of Sacrifices, where offerings were once transported to Aldrich, Saint of the Deep.

title: Anri of Astora
snippet:
If Anri does not die in the Catacombs, they can next be encountered in Irithyll of the Boreal Valley, at the Church of Yorshka. Here the player can learn Quiet Resolve through dialogue, and Anri will gift them the Ring of the Evil Eye here should they have left the Catacombs without finding out about Horace's fate. Again, Anri's questline can diverge here, depending on action taken against the assassin hidden within the Church of Yorshka:

#If the assassin is killed, Anri will continue on to the final phase of the questline, but Yuria of Londor's questline will end.
#If the assassin is spared, Anri will die at her hand and the questline will end, however Yuria's will continue.

The final part of the questline will begin once Pontiff Sulyvahn has been defeated.

 notes : Offering Rosaria's Fingers any Pale Tongues immediately ends Sirris' questline, and prevents the player from obtaining any further rewards from it. Sirris' questline will be available again in NG+, as long as the player doesn't offer tongues after starting NG+.
**Because of this, it's impossible to obtain both the Proper Bow gesture from summoning Yellowfinger Heysel and the Silvercat Ring from helping Sirris against Creighton the Wanderer in the same NG cycle. Due to the significant benefits the Silvercat Ring provides, players may want to wait until NG+ to obtain the gesture. The Darkmoon Loyalty gesture, and by extension the Blade of the Darkmoon covenant item, can still be obtained in the same NG cycle as Proper Bow by giving the Dreamchaser's Ashes to the Shrine Handmaid and talking to Sirris prior to offering the tongue.

title: Symbol of Avarice (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Symbol of Avarice (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - armor - how_to_obtain 
 how_to_obtain : The Symbol of Avarice is a potential drop from all Mimics encountered throughout the course of the game. It may even be obtained from the very first Mimic in the High Wall of Lothric. All Mimics have guaranteed drops, but they may also yield a Symbol of Avarice along with these.

Since Mimics are non-respawning enemies, each encounter with one is very valuable if one is looking to obtain a Symbol of Avarice. The player must first make sure their Item Discovery attribute is as high as possible. Crushing a Rusted Coin, or even a Rusted Gold Coin, before engaging a Mimic is recommended, as well as equipping the Covetous Gold Serpent Ring.

title: Greirat of the Undead Settlement
snippet:
Greirat of the Undead Settlement -  Dark Souls III - character - questline 
 questline : After thanking the Ashen One for freeing him, Greirat asks a favor; he bestows the Blue Tearstone Ring to the player under the condition that they find and give it to a woman named Loretta who lives somewhere in the Undead Settlement. He then warps to Firelink Shrine and offers mercantile services.

Loretta's Bone is found on a body hanging from the balcony of the first three-story building encountered in the Undead Settlement. It can be knocked down by attacking it with a weapon or projectile. Once the player collects the item and gives it to Greirat, he allows them to keep the ring. After this, Greirat's services will become temporarily unavailable as he grieves for Loretta. Interacting with him after reloading the area will bestow the "Curl up" gesture. The player needs to reload the area again in order for him to return to normal.

snippet:
Yoel of Londor -  Dark Souls III - character - questline 
 questline : Yoel is first encountered near the beginning of the Undead Settlement, at the edge of a crumbled bridge. The only survivor among many other less fortunate pilgrims like him, he seems enlightened to be in the presence of the Ashen One and asks if he could be allowed in their service. Agreeing to his plea will make him move to Firelink Shrine. There, he can be found on the lowermost level, at the end of the right corridor past Greirat, where he will sell an assortment of Sorceries to the player. Refusing his service will result in Yoel remaining in this spot, waiting for the Ashen One to change their mind.

Selecting the "Talk" option while in his interaction menu will teach the player the "Beckon" gesture. As a former sorcerer, all of his wares are sorceries.

snippet:
Dark Wood Grain Ring -  Dark Souls - ring - availability

Joining the covenant causes Shiva of the East and his invisible bodyguard to spawn, just outside of Alvina's location in the direction of the sealed door. The bodyguard is standing very close to the cliff, and when killed will always drop the ring; but killing him will betray the covenant and make all NPCs hostile again, which can be reverted through absolving your sins at Oswald of Carim in the Undead Parish.

title: Giant Archer of the Undead Settlement
snippet:
Giant Archer of the Undead Settlement -  Dark Souls III - character - strategy 
 strategy : Upon meeting and possibly befriending the giant, the player will have two choices: either let their new friend live to aid them while traversing a few dangerous areas in the game, or kill him to obtain the Hawk Ring.

If the latter option has been chosen, then he may be challenged at the top of his tower in the Undead Settlement; an easy task due to the small space where he is encountered at and which will severely compromise his mobility. In addition, the nearby staircase will provide complete cover from all of his attacks. The giant drops the Hawk Ring upon defeat, an accessory that allows arrows to travel a longer distance.

title: Ending (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
** Yoel is now dead, and Yuria of Londor will have moved into Firelink Shrine next to his body, informing the player that Anri is being guided by one of her fellows.
Further into the Catacombs, speak with Anri on a spot to the side of the bridge leading to High Lord Wolnir. If talked to a second time, they will ask if the player knows where Horace is; Horace is located down a tunnel in Smouldering Lake, although the questline does not require the player to ever encounter the now-hollowed Horace.
** If the player says they have not seen Horace (which remains an option even if they have), Anri will not find him and depart the Catacombs, continuing the questline.
** If the player kills the hollowed Horace and then tells Anri where he is (or goes to kill Horace right after giving Anri his location, without reloading any area), Anri will find Horace's body, build a grave in his memory and depart the Catacombs, continuing the questline.

title: Orbeck of Vinheim
snippet:
Learning Sorceries from Orbeck will yield various rewards. Once the player has learned any four Sorceries and has given him at least one Sorcery scroll, Orbeck will gift them the Young Dragon Ring, provided that they did not start off as the Sorcerer class. After learning Aural Decoy, Farron Flashsword, Spook and Pestilent Mist, Orbeck will teach the player the "Silent Ally" gesture, and gift them the Slumbering Dragoncrest Ring.

When both Orbeck and Yuria of Londor are present at Firelink Shrine, Yuria will claim that Orbeck has proclaimed himself Lord of Hollows, and request that the player deal with Orbeck. The player may choose to kill Orbeck at any time and present his ashes to Yuria in exchange for the Morion Blade, or spare him in order to complete his questline and obtain his ashes much later.

title: Amnesiac Lapp
snippet:
Amnesiac Lapp -  Dark Souls III - character - questline 
 questline : Lapp is a hollow who has forgotten his past, even his own name. Eventually, he asks the player if they've seen the Purging Monument, in hopes that he can remember his former identity. The player can find Lapp throughout the Ringed City. He will give the player a toast most times.

Once the player has found the Purging Monument, they can go tell Lapp and he will thank the player. He also promises to remember the player as a friend, no matter what. If the player has exhausted Lapp's dialogue several times and has not told him about the whereabouts of the Purging Monument prior to fighting Gael, he will become hollow and attack the player on sight.

title: High Wall of Lothric
snippet:
Towards the end of the area, the player will encounter High Priestess Emma, who grants them the Small Lothric Banner and Way of Blue covenant.

The area has two bosses: Vordt of the Boreal Valley, who guards the entrance to the Undead Settlement, and the Dancer of the Boreal Valley, who guards the entrance to Lothric Castle. Although the Dancer is intended to be fought much later in the game, players can face her early by killing Emma.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - high_wall_of_lothric 
 high_wall_of_lothric : The Ashen One then progresses through the High Wall of Lothric, now home to mindless hollow soldiers, knights, and a fire-breathing wyvern. Fighting their way to a church, they encounter Emma, the high priestess of Lothric Castle. Emma provides them with a banner that will allow them safe passage to the Undead Settlement, but warns them that their path is guarded by Vordt of the Boreal Valley. Emma also gives the opportunity to join the Way of Blue covenant. Also in the High Wall is Greirat of the Undead Settlement, a thief that will swear himself to the Ashen One if they rescue him from his cell and promises to look for a woman named Loretta in the Undead Settlement.

After finding and defeating Vordt, the Ashen One raises the banner on a ledge, and is transported by Batwing Demons to the Undead Settlement, a dilapidated town inhabited by hollows.

title: Yoel of Londor
snippet: Yoel's dead body will be on the same spot he was when the Ashen One last saw him; uncharacteristically, his dead body will always remain, unless the player killed him themselves. If his questline was completed, Yuria will be next to his body, selling his old wares and allowing for the questline to continue. It is of note that killing Yoel after obtaining all five Dark Sigils does not void the questline, although there are no benefits to doing so.
